Chapter 10: Legacy and Reckoning
As the decade came to an end, that big question of legacy was on everyone’s mind. What would those eight years of hope—and struggle—really mean for the future? Would we actually learn from what we’d been through, or were we just doomed to go in circles and make the same mistakes all over again?
Everywhere you looked, folks were wrestling with those questions. Picture a college student, fired up by the activism around her, asking herself if real change is even possible. And just down the block, there’s her older neighbor—someone who’s seen plenty of promises come and go—gently warning her not to expect too much.
The truth is, the legacy of that era? It’s still being written. Sure, we saw real progress—the kind you can actually feel. But let’s be honest, there were setbacks too. The backlash got loud, but so did the resistance. The story isn’t finished; it’s being shaped every single day by the choices people make.
Building a more just and equal world? It’s never a walk in the park. It takes guts. It takes sticking with it, even when things get tough. And it means refusing to settle for the easy way out. If there’s one thing the past makes clear, it’s this: progress can happen, but it’s never a sure thing. The struggle goes on, carried forward by everyone who chooses not to give up.
